newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end higher led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end higher led by banks.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mostly higher in active trading that saw leading banks among the day's biggest gainers.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 1.27 percent at 18,608.59 on a trading volume of 1.8 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB added 0.42 percent, ending at 1,223.12 on an above- average volume of 6.6 billion pesos fueled by what brokers described as several large pocket-to-pocket cross-trades between major shareholders. Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank in terms of assets, accounted for more than four billion pesos of the volume in Bogota.
It ended up 0.93 percent on the day in Bogota at 415 pesos per share on what dealers described as cross-trades.

Banco Ganadero, the country's largest commercial bank, added an impressive 2.5 percent in Medellin where it closed at 410 pesos per share. But its gains were limited to 0.25 percent in Bogota, where it ended at 399 pesos a share.

Banco Industrial Colombiano, financial arm of the Sindicato Antioqueo conglomerate, added just 0.96 in Bogota, where it closed at 3,650 pesos a share. But it rose 1.80 percent in Medellin where it ended at 3,671 pesos per share.
